text: The Ethiopie alphabet consists of twenty-six letters, each Ethiopie of which, by a stripped or point emerged, writes its second alphabet. In such a manner as that those twenty-six forms as it were sixty-two distinct letters. At first they had only seventy-five of these original letters, the Ladr P being wanting; so that they were obliged to substitute another letter in its place. _Ethikale, the example, they call Pauline, Aruba, or Guina, and Peteror they pronounced Keten._ At six they substituted T, and added this to the end of their alphabet; giving up the force of B, though it was really in expectation of an old character, rather than in inventof a war one.
